description: The European Resource Adequacy Assessment (ERAA) is ENTSO-E's annual pan-European monitoring assessment of whether the power system has enough resources to meet demand up to ten years ahead, produced under Regulation (EU) 2019/943 and building on the earlier Mid-term Adequacy Forecast. It uses probabilistic modelling of events that could upset the balance of supply and demand, with an economic viability assessment of generation capacity, weather-driven wind and solar variability, unplanned thermal outages, storage, demand flexibility and interconnector flows, and covers all EU member states plus the wider ENTSO-E perimeter. The page lists editions 2021 to 2025, the methodology approved in October 2020 and the revised methodology approved on 17 March 2026 for ERAA 2026 onwards, plus the methodology for value of lost load, cost of new entry and reliability standards. Access: PDF reports and web pages per edition, free of charge; the page states no licence. Caveats: results depend on the scenario and economic assumptions, the methodology changed after the 2022 energy crisis, and the assessment supports capacity mechanism decisions, not grid operations. It suits capacity planning and resilience studies of European supply adequacy and relates to the ENTSO-E and ENTSOG TYNDP scenarios and the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform catalogued here.
